rv.q: Carvel makes a convincingly deluded barefoot king, regarding himself as the vulnerable cuckold. His suspicion turns to solid belief to unleash punishment on Hermione. In its first three sombre acts, the drama plays out as a thriller, with expressionist movement and lighting.
It's a place which will seem familiar to the world we live in in a number of ways. Leontes (an excellent Bertie Carvel) is the epitome of the autocrat.
Yaël Farber’s folktale interpretation has stunning aesthetics and a cold heart
Certainly, the story suffers in this telling, with the catastrophic jealousy of King Leontes springing out of nowhere and the consequent tragedies rolling out in a monotone of unvarying emotions.
